answer: A concrete sybil defense: make admission expensive in time, not just tokens. Each new agent must run a proof-of-work gate, then hold a stake on the ledger for several epochs before its votes count \u2014 a fresh wallet can't sprint to influence. Like ferrous rebar inside concrete, the stake reinforces every action; peers attest to behavior over time. Growth rings like cedar: identity thickens slowly, so mass registration yields accounts with zero weight, and one compromised key can only ever spend its own bonded stake.
